task: MC-P0 independent review of comprehensive-fix candidate

findings.title: safeInternalPath returns a protocol-relative URL for "..//host" payloads
where: used at apps/frontend/src/app/(app)/matters/[matterId]/work/[itemId]/page.tsx:55 and rendered at :109 as <Link href={from}>
findings.evidence: V4 (the real function): input "/..//evil.test" yields "//evil.test". The guard "!raw.startsWith('//')" runs on the raw input; the new URL() step resolves ".." and leaves a path that starts with "//", and no check is applied to the output. The page then renders href="//evil.test", so the "Back" link leaves the site. Reachable with ?from=/..//evil.test on /matters/{m}/work/{item} for a signed-in user who clicks Back.
findings.login_path: safeReturnTo (flow.ts:96-113) has the same defect (V5) but is neutralised: beginLogin, the login route and resolveReturnTo (flow.ts:116-118, used by the callback) re-validate, and the second pass rejects "//evil.test". Defense in depth, not a fix.
findings.relation_to_delta: Pre-existing code, not introduced by the delta. The delta added dot-segment cases to paths.test.ts and flow.test.ts that pass but cover only "/x/../login" style inputs, so they give false assurance about the output; the author packet entry EX-03 ("redirect safety: no finding") is wrong and is superseded by this finding.
findings.minimal_fix_not_applied: After computing the path in both functions, reject any output that starts with "//" or "/\\" (return the fallback); add "/..//evil.test", "/x/..//evil.test", "/%2e%2e//evil.test" and "/..///evil.test" to both tests, red before the fix. Source edits are outside this review mode.

findings.title: bad-request at preview: mostly a fixable sheet, but not only
findings.evidence: Sources of 400 bad-request on import/preview: (a) port.ErrSheetInvalid from parseSheet (dataops_service.go:443-466): format, byte limit, decode error, empty sheet, missing required column, row limit; user-fixable, except "format" which the UI cannot send wrongly. (b) readSheetUpload errBadRequest (data_handlers.go:141,147,151): malformed multipart, missing or duplicate "file" part; client/transport faults. The two share urn:mc:bad-request and McError drops the problem detail, so the frontend cannot tell them apart. The comment in actions.ts that a preview can draw "only" an unreadable spreadsheet overclaims; the message shown ("The file could not be read. Nothing was stored.") stays true because preview writes nothing.
findings.commit_path: importCommitAction is unchanged: a 400 there is shown as the generic error. The catch calls endAttempt(session, attempt) without results (actions.ts:166), so the attempt stays retained and unresolved (pending-attempts.ts:70-81); that behaviour is pre-existing and outside the delta.
findings.recommendation: Soften the code comment; optionally keep the problem detail in McError so (a) and (b) can be told apart later.

findings.title: The seam test proves the action result, not the rendered state
findings.evidence: The new test drives fetch to McError to the action result through the real seam (not an implementation branch), which is what CR-001 changed. No component test renders a failed preview: import-section.tsx:186-198 shows previewError in an Alert, and fieldErrors.file is unused by the UI. data-transfer-ui.test.tsx has no failed-preview case.

findings.title: read-failure-callers.test.ts can miss a misplaced partial
findings.evidence: V6: the scan regex /<ReadFailure\b[^>]*?\/>/ does not match a tag whose attributes contain ">" (for example an arrow function or a comparison), and cannot see a partial passed through {...props} or an aliased import. Today all 31 tags in 15 files match and exactly one carries partial, so the guard is correct now; the failure mode is fail-open for the security direction.
findings.recommendation: Parse with the TypeScript compiler API or add a negative test that the scan found every "<ReadFailure" occurrence (count of "<ReadFailure" equals count of matched tags).

findings.title: Primary versus partial handling, re-grant, limitation
findings.evidence: read-failure.tsx purges for sign-in always and for forbidden/not-found unless partial. 31 <ReadFailure call sites in 15 files; exactly one passes partial (work/[itemId]/page.tsx:275, the proof section, a nested read after the primary Promise.all at :59-92 succeeded). drafts.test.tsx covers purge per kind, keep for unavailable/error, partial keep, sign-in with partial purges, and no revival after re-grant (20+ cases pass in V3). Whole-tab purge is documented as CR-003 and not described as per-Matter.
findings.residual: F4-F6 of the earlier review (window between reads, purge after hydration, unobserved revoke and re-grant) remain accepted limitations.

findings.title: CR-002 stays a product decision; the author did not waive it
findings.evidence: intent-form.tsx:62 keeps the key in useState and :69 the frozen payload in a ref; document-forms.tsx:61 does the same for the upload key. Contract rev 12 section 0 guarantees reload survival only for bulk/import; zcode-handoff.md:95 says a retry under a new key is disabled. A reload loses the attempt, so a re-submit can use a new key. That backend creation commands are deduplicated by key only was not verified beyond the contract table.
options: B server-side session slot plus contract revision
